findings.description: `pip install` of unpinned package(s) uv in Dockerfile at line 3. Without an exact version the next install silently picks up whatever is published, including a compromised release.
findings.recommendation: Pin an exact version (pkg@1.2.3, pkg==1.2.3) and prefer a lockfile or hash-checked requirements.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Universal search tool supporting all SerpApi engines and result types.

    When to use:
        - Any query needing live, structured SERP data: web results, news, product listings, job postings, local businesses, flight/hotel prices, video results, images, stock/weather cards, knowledge graph entities.
    
    Engine discovery via MCP resources:
        - serpapi://engines lists all engines supported by this tool.
        - serpapi://engines/<engine> provides engine-specific parameters and supported options.
        - Example: serpapi://engines/google_news

    Input schema:
        params: JSON object containing SerpApi engine parameters.
            Common parameters:
                - q: Search query. Required for most engines.
                - engine: SerpApi engine name. Defaults to "google_light".
                - location: Optional geographic location for localized results.
                - output: Optional response format. Omit for JSON (default), or set to "md" for Markdown.
    
            Engine-specific parameters are available via MCP resources:
                - serpapi://engines lists all supported engines.
                - serpapi://engines/<engine> provides parameters and options for one engine.
    
        mode: Response mode. Defaults to "complete".
            - "complete": Return the full SerpApi response.
            - "compact": Remove metadata fields from JSON responses. Markdown is returned unchanged.
    
    Output schema:
        structuredContent.result contains the response string: serialized JSON or unchanged Markdown.
        The same string is included in text content. Tool failures preserve this wrapper and set isError to true.

    Guided search:
        Searches can request missing engine parameters from supporting clients using the engine catalog and engine-specific rules.
        Flights collect airports and dates, hotels collect the destination and stay dates, and directions collect missing endpoints.
        Other clients receive a missing-parameter error. Cancellation does not run a search.

    Examples:
        Weather: {"params": {"q": "weather in London", "engine": "google"}, "mode": "complete"}
        Stock: {"params": {"q": "AAPL stock", "engine": "google"}, "mode": "complete"}
        General: {"params": {"q": "coffee shops", "engine": "google_light", "location": "Austin, TX"}, "mode": "complete"}
        Compact: {"params": {"q": "news"}, "mode": "compact"}
        Markdown: {"params": {"q": "news", "output": "md"}}

    Supported engines include (not limited to):
        - google
        - google_light
        - google_flights
        - google_hotels
        - google_images
        - google_news
        - google_local
        - google_shopping
        - google_jobs
        - bing
        - yahoo
        - duckduckgo
        - youtube_search
        - baidu
        - ebay

tools.name: extract
tools.description:
Extract content from a public http(s) URL, discover site URLs, or crawl pages.

API options go in params: url is required; params.mode is scrape (default), map, or crawl. See serpapi://engines/extract for all options.

Top-level mode controls the response:
- complete (default): full JSON.
- compact: native Markdown by default.

params.output selects the format and overrides either default:
- "md": return native Markdown unchanged in either response mode.
- "json": return JSON, with filtering determined by the response mode.

Compact JSON removes metadata. For scrape responses containing markdown, it also keeps only markdown and any error field. include_markdown=false or an explicit json_restrictor skips this extra filtering. Map/crawl and responses without markdown keep their remaining fields. Use complete with output="json" for full JSON.

Crawl max_pages defaults to 10 (maximum 100). Each successfully extracted, uncached page consumes one credit.

Examples:
Full scrape JSON: {"params":{"url":"https://example.com"},"mode":"complete"}
Scrape Markdown: {"params":{"url":"https://example.com"},"mode":"compact"}
Map URLs as JSON: {"params":{"url":"https://example.com","mode":"map"},"mode":"complete"}
Crawl pages as Markdown: {"params":{"url":"https://example.com","mode":"crawl","max_pages":2},"mode":"compact"}

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
